text:
Calgary arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 6-2 win over SEA that made them 4-1-0 in their last five. They're missing Connor Zary, Brennan Othmann and Samuel Honzek. Colorado, 2-3-0 in its last five, has had two days off since a 5-2 win over NJD that ended the Devils' four-game winning streak, and is without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. These two met on Oct 8, and COL won 7-3.

Our numbers favor Colorado, with a projected 3.41 goals to 2.59. At five on five, COL has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against CGY's 47%. Calgary's record flatters its underlying play less than you'd think: a -13 goal difference on -5.1 expected, so finishing and goaltending have cost them. Colorado is the reverse, with finishing doing the lifting. On special teams, COL has the edge on both sides, and CGY takes 4.6 penalties a game. Projected goalie Mackenzie Blackwood has a .894 save percentage this season, though he saved 8.01 goals above expected last year. Calgary's starter isn't confirmed.

Nathan MacKinnon is 41% to score and 85% for a point. As Corey Masisak of the Denver Post posted, he had "2.0-0.4 in expected goals" at even strength in his last game. For Calgary, Matt Coronato is 55% for a point after a four-point night. Among our under-the-radar picks, Nicolas Roy is 12% to score on dangerous fourth-line shots, and T.J. Hughes is 40% for a point.
